response: We agree that numerical reproducibility and a MEMOTE score alone cannot establish predictive biological validity. The revision now tests biomass mass closure and precursor producibility, maintenance and uptake sensitivity, closed-boundary energy generation, loop-free exchange extrema, global GPR effects and transfer dependence. Original JGI inputs are recovered and all 477 model genes have sequence-supported public-locus mappings. The response below identifies the actual curation and the remaining biochemical evidence gaps; we do not present this draft as an experimentally validated strain-specific reference model.

We have performed additional computational work rather than relying solely on limitations text: full-reaction blockage classification, 432 certified loopless exchange endpoints, precursor-demand and biomass-mass tests, sequence-supported annotation of all model genes, and global GPR deletion tests. We also built a new inclusion-minimal subset of the reactions added after the recovered original draft, retaining 112 of 237 added reactions while disabling 125; native growth remains 0.688 h^-1. All tested OK2-OK4 gene implementations remain non-growing in this reduced network. This subset is a diagnostic sensitivity model, not a globally smallest or uniquely biological gapfill. Related-strain amino-acid measurements ground a mass-preserved biomass candidate. Functional GPR specificity and target-strain biomass measurements remain unresolved; these tests do not by themselves establish the journal standard for a fully curated GEM.

The phrase has been removed from the current manuscript. We describe a gapseq-derived draft reconstruction gapfilled using the stated anaerobic medium and simulated under explicitly defined nutrient constraints. The Methods also state that using the same medium for gapfilling and simulation makes baseline growth expected by construction.

C. sporogenes is retained only as a functional comparator for characterized reductive amino-acid gene-cluster architecture. It is not used as a close phylogenetic comparator. The 20%, 33%, 50%, 66% and 100% values are archived gutSMASH KnownClusterBlast fractions of reference-cluster genes with homologs, not pairwise amino-acid identities or query-alignment coverage. Table 2 uses one consistent term, candidate match, and gives the observed reference-gene fraction without treating a universal fraction as proof of an intact pathway. Separately, the new reviewed-reference DIAMOND candidate flag requires at least 30% identity and at least 70% coverage on both query and subject. All alignment values and provisional functional decisions are supplied in S54/S61. The archived gutSMASH invocation does not establish a separate custom per-hit coverage cutoff; none is invented.

The recovered gapseq output and pinned source resolve this point more precisely than the earlier response. At recorded commit c64db99b, both pathway and transporter searches default to 75% reference-query coverage and explicitly pass the filter to BLAST/DIAMOND. In the original files, all 20,283 reaction-table rows with recorded coverage and all 10,613 transporter rows have 75-100% coverage; none is below 75%. The Methods now report this evidence alongside the bit-score threshold of 200. Complete historical command-line recovery is not claimed. Reference-query coverage is distinguished from subject coverage and from gutSMASH cluster coverage.

The Discussion now explains why both calculations are needed. pFBA selects a representative minimum-total-flux state after optimizing biomass. It does not establish a unique secretion phenotype. FVA reports the feasible range of each selected exchange under a stated growth requirement; broad nitrogen/sulfur ranges and zero-butyrate states limit claims based on a single pFBA point. Selected loopless endpoints additionally test whether internal cycles explain those ranges.

The Methods define derivation_factor as the dimensionless multiplier in maxFlux = base_maxFlux * derivation_factor. It is a controlled perturbation of assumed model uptake capacity, not an empirical uptake measurement. The six-amino-acid multipliers derive from High-protein/EU-average AGORA ratios, whose dietary supply scale differs from the organism exchange-capacity scale.

The active manuscript cites external benchmarking as S5-S6. The current consolidated supplementary index maps every S1-S73 identifier to explicit files and labels historical aliases. The immutable baseline benchmarking PDF retains the older S11/S14/S2 labels as historical provenance only; it is not an additional current supplement. Current S11 and S14 denote the carbon screen and production envelope, and the new sequence figure is Supplementary Figure S1. Figures 1 and 2 have been regenerated with separated legends, titles and annotations. The package now includes concrete annotation, biomass, looplessness, precursor and GPR sensitivity work, including the new reduced added-reaction subset. We have not equated removal of every condition-inactive reaction with biological curation: a reaction can be inactive because its substrate is absent, and unsupported deletion would conceal rather than resolve uncertainty. The primary annotation derivative preserves deposited chemistry, while mechanistic and biomass changes remain evidence-labelled candidates. We acknowledge that further biochemical/experimental curation may still be required for acceptance.

We agree with the central concern. The revised study no longer treats the archived high-butyrate reaction deletions as viable engineering designs or a feasible lactate exchange as evidence of necessary cross-feeding. Global GPR knockouts eliminate the attractive OK2-OK4 phenotypes, and donor-lactate-export blocking preserves the selected community growth states. The remaining conclusions concern constraint-dependent model behavior and robustness to explicit counterfactuals.

MJR8396C is now identified as a vaginal isolate at the start of the Abstract and Introduction and in the genome Methods. Gut-like media and the bifidobacterial partner are imposed model scenarios. We do not claim documented intestinal colonization, obesity association, fiber response or complex-carbohydrate degradation for this strain. The earlier inappropriate strain-specific citation argument is removed; related-strain physiology is identified explicitly as contextual evidence. The title describes a constraint-based analysis rather than an established gut ecological role.

Accession-matched sequence bytes were analyzed. Reciprocal skani/FastANI and both alignment fractions are supplied for DSM 20460, NM10, BL7 and closer reference genomes. skani ANI to the physiological comparators is 82.73-82.86%, with approximately 43-47% alignment fractions; it is not evidence of conspecificity. The exact assembly is assigned Megasphaera sp001546855 in GTDB R232, labelled as a release lookup rather than a newly run GTDB-Tk classification. Genome statistics are measured directly and plotted in Supplementary Figure S1: original JGI 2,426,262 bp/51.04337% GC and public assembly 2,453,897 bp/51.02898% canonical-base GC. The former comparative Figure 3 has been replaced by the current biomass/quality figure; the new sequence figure supplies the requested measurements without mixing assembly versions.

The Results now report the joint lactate mismatch, including growth, acetate/propionate, CO2 and product partitioning, and withdraw the cross-medium 13% accuracy comparison. The 88 pathway diagnostics and maintenance/biomass sensitivities test dependence on LDH-Etf, PFOR, Bcd-Etf, acrylate/CoA connectivity, GAM and an explicitly hypothetical racemase. Bcd-Etf bifurcating stoichiometry is already represented in rxn90001; adding another generic reaction would duplicate it. Restrictions and racemase addition alter growth and partitioning but do not establish a unique causal repair. Native Rnf/PFOR/acrylate flux ranges and acetate CoA-transferase flows are now supplied in S68/S72. No unsupported directionality/GPR change is promoted merely to fit the related-strain maximum. Lactate-dependent physiological and engineering conclusions are downgraded.

Predicted biomass fluxes are explicitly uptake-constrained theoretical optima. Baseline growth is expected because the same medium was used for gapfilling, and gapfill non-uniqueness is acknowledged. The deposited template is bacterial Gram-negative, appropriate as a stated template for this diderm lineage but not measured composition. We report uptake, GAM/NGAM and mass-preserved composition sensitivities (282 inherited scenarios), additional sequence/related-strain candidates, precursor tests, closed-boundary energy probes and 432 certified loopless exchange endpoints. Native COBRApy selected-exchange FVA is supplied at 90%, 99% and 100% growth for all three media; the manuscript directs readers from the nutrient-flux table to these intervals. Nitrogen/sulfur point values are not treated as uniquely determined. These checks do not calibrate absolute rates to culture measurements.

We correct the flux basis explicitly: at 50:50 abundance the two taxon-specific glucose fluxes sum to 20 before weighting, but correspond to 10 mmol per community gDW per hour after multiplication by 0.5. Matched monocultures distinguish the same total-biomass supply from the full-pool-per-member allocation. Five abundances, four tradeoffs and twelve donor/medium controls were evaluated; all 240 cases were independently completed through native MICOM with a documented custom QP adapter, and 540 QP-conditioned exchange-FVA ranges are supplied. Nearly equal member rates at equal abundance are explained by the quadratic regularizer. Both-member growth persists when donor D/L-lactate exports are blocked, including without external lactate; no universal coculture advantage is claimed. The donor is 22L. A strain-matched study measures total lactate production, but does not validate D-lactate production or net L-lactate consumption. Those stereochemical fluxes remain unsupported model behavior; uptake/D-LDH restrictions and no-external-lactate controls are therefore sensitivities, not evidence of the observed organism.

The source GPRs, target gene counts and all gene-associated reactions are reported. Gene 2776381411 supports both GMP synthesis alternatives, and 2776381538 both CTP synthesis alternatives. Reaction deletion leaves a same-gene bypass; global gene deletion does not. Every tested minimal gene implementation of OK2-OK4 abolishes growth in the full deposited model and the new reduced added-reaction subset. The latter retains 112 of 237 reactions absent from the recovered original draft, disables 125, and passes an inclusion-minimality certificate at a stated 0.1 h^-1 growth floor; it is not a global minimum-cardinality or historical weighted gapfill reconstruction. OK2/OK3 are identified as adjacent-pathway counterfactuals, not independent strategies. The intervention table now includes WT and all ten archived designs including OK0/OK1, which are labelled archived deletion scenarios rather than successful production strategies. Recovered tilt settings include bio1 - 0.001 EX_cpd00211_e0, 78 candidates, unit costs, maximum cost two, five solutions, 1800 s and 25% WT growth floor. Growth/product envelopes and worst-case butyrate reject guaranteed growth coupling.

The racemase explanation is withdrawn: no direct racemase is represented in the deposited MJR8396C model. A hypothetical addition changes the phenotype and remains a sensitivity because activity and maturation are unverified. The six-Asp/Gly/Lys/Met/Cys/His panel is described as selected medium components, not a canonical Stickland donor/acceptor test; effects up to 0.00225 h^-1 are numerical departures from additivity without biological synergy claims. Protein-rich and fiber-response interpretations are removed. Acetate alone and acetate supplied with glucose are different backgrounds. New native glucose-conditioned calculations show acetate uptake increasing growth from 0.613 to 0.631 h^-1 and butyrate from 8.76 to 11.1 at capacity 5; butanoyl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase flux increases with butyrate. This is an explicit model co-substrate mechanism, not experimental confirmation of an electron-sink mechanism.

Table 2 now defines percentages as reference-cluster gene coverage, not amino-acid identity. All archived matches use consistent candidate-match terminology; 20/33/50% values are not elevated to confirmed complete pathways. A new explicit concordance table separates reaction representation, provisional sequence/GPR evidence and flux feasibility. Native pFBA and 90%-growth FVA for Rnf, PFOR and the acrylate steps are listed by medium (S68). For example, gut-like Rnf spans 1.95-37.2 and PFOR -30.4 to 1.46 in the signed SBML direction. C5/C6 end-product formation/export is not represented as a completed fermentative phenotype. Existing fatty-acid biosynthetic intermediates do not establish chain elongation; absence of model end-product routes does not establish absence of the genes. Sequence candidates and incomplete biochemical/database mapping remain explicit.

Published iME375 from DSM 20460 and six authoritative AGORA2 Megasphaera models were obtained and simulated under their deposited settings and an explicit mapped anaerobic substrate panel, including L/D lactate and acetate sensitivity. Growth/no-growth, product spectra and selected-exchange FVA are supplied. The iME375 deposited objective is product oriented and its biomass/source coefficients differ; several AGORA models have unresolved biomass conventions and nutrient dependencies in the common medium. Minimum-extra-import LPs expose these dependencies without selective rescue or invented gapfill. These results provide transparent qualitative model comparisons, but do not support an absolute-growth or matched-coculture ranking. Such calibration remains an unresolved request rather than a completed physiological validation.

All 477 deposited genes now have sequence-supported public protein/locus mappings, and the annotation-only primary SBML adds NCBI protein cross-references and locus notes. We do not invent UniProt/KEGG functional assignments to improve a score. Historical MEMOTE is explicitly labelled and was not recomputed. Among assessable fully annotated internal reactions, the mass/charge audit detects zero imbalances; 195 MJR8396C and 147 partner internal reactions have incomplete/non-specific formulas and are reported separately. No unsupported proton-balance change was made.

The current revision tests rather than assumes the proposed lactate mechanism. Native community controls show that the selected growth states persist after donor lactate-export blocking, and global gene deletions overturn the attractive reaction-only engineering interpretation. We report conditional exchange in an imposed nutrient setting and do not present the simulations as verification of the organisms in coculture.

We have added an explicit pathway-concordance table, native Rnf/PFOR/acrylate flux ranges, original-JGI-to-model mappings and reviewed-reference evidence. A cluster hit alone does not specify balanced reaction chemistry, substrate specificity, multisubunit GPR logic or required maturation. We therefore do not add reactions simply to make all gutSMASH predictions flux feasible. Already represented Bcd-Etf/Rnf chemistry is identified, and incomplete amino-acid/C5-C6 routes remain candidate curation targets. Unsupported pathway addition remains unperformed; the response does not claim a complete genome-to-GEM biochemical reconciliation.

We agree that a strain-specific comparative phenotype claim requires the requested matched analyses. NM10 and BL7 are included in the reciprocal ANI and direct sequence statistics. The authorized local search found no runnable NM10/BL7 SBML files, and the 2013 comparative paper describes ModelSEED drafts without supplying runnable models among the retrieved supplements. We have not substituted another strain or a newly automated reconstruction for these exact models. The full NM10/BL7 medium, intervention and bifidobacterial-coculture suite remains unperformed. We have removed claims that the present model establishes uniquely strain-specific phenotypic divergence; a six-model AGORA2/iME375 diagnostic comparison is reported with calibration limits. This specific reviewer request remains open.

The Discussion now unifies these analyses as tests of whether engineering or community predictions survive counterfactual controls. The attractive OK2-OK4 reaction deletions are not supported gene-edit designs, and the community does not demonstrate obligatory lactate transfer, mutualism or a general advantage over a same-supply monoculture. Consequently we do not rank an engineered monoculture against a synthetic mutualistic coculture as viable bioprocesses. A practical comparison would require gene-validated viable interventions, experimentally characterized partners, matched nutrient supply and measured productivity/yield; the present calculations delimit those hypotheses rather than establish process superiority.

The partner is B. adolescentis 22L, assembly GCF_000737885.1 paired with GCA_000737885.1 and chromosome CP007443.1. The recovered source SBML filename identifies that accession, its SHA256 matches the deposited partner byte-for-byte, and official NCBI metadata confirms 22L (BioSample SAMN02673695; human-milk isolation). Duranti et al. characterize starch metabolism in this strain. Turroni et al. 2015 experimentally report its total lactate production during glycan fermentation, using HPLC with lactic-acid calibration, but do not establish enantiomer-specific D production or net L-lactate uptake. We found no strain-specific experiment verifying those two modeled capabilities. We therefore retain them as unresolved behavior and report no-external-lactate, donor-export, uptake and D-LDH sensitivity controls rather than treating model flux as validation.
